title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All directors (and their Associates), senior management, and Key Management Personnel (AASB 124) of Waypoint REIT; and all employees and contractors or consultants required to comply with Waypoint REIT's policies or considered appropriate by the Chair and Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Relevant Persons
tiers.description: Restricted Persons together with their Associates; the operative population bound by insider trading, Closed Period, no-speculative-trading, protection arrangements and security/margin lending rules.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A spouse (including de facto), child (including step-child or adopted child), close relative, financially dependent person, or a company, trust, partnership or other entity that a Restricted Person (or the above persons) controls or significantly influences.

tiers.name: Chair
tiers.description: The Chair of the Board; distinguished for clearance (own dealings cleared by the Audit and Risk Management Committee chair) and as an approver for other directors' Closed Period exceptional-circumstances dealing.

tiers.name: Chair and his or her Associates
tiers.description: The Chair and his or her Associates, as a distinct row in the ordinary clearance table: cleared by the chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee.

tiers.name: All Relevant Persons other than the Chair and his or her Associates
tiers.description: Every Relevant Person other than the Chair and his or her Associates, for ordinary clearance purposes: cleared by the Chair.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Waypoint REIT, distinguished for Closed Period exceptional-circumstances approval: the Chair of the Board determines whether the exception applies.

tiers.name: Employees, contractors and Relevant Persons other than directors
tiers.description: All employees, contractors and other Relevant Persons who are not directors, distinguished for Closed Period exceptional-circumstances approval: the Managing Director and CEO determines whether the exception applies.

tiers.name: All Employees
tiers.description: All Waypoint REIT employees, whether or not a Restricted Person; must seek approval to deal during a Board-imposed blackout period even if not otherwise subject to the Policy's ordinary clearance requirement.

definitions.hedging_definition: operate to limit the economic risk of any Relevant Persons security holding (e.g., hedging arrangements) including Waypoint REIT securities held beneficially (for example, on trust or under any incentive plan) on that Relevant Persons behalf

windows.start_anchor: the day any price sensitive information is released to the ASX
windows.end_anchor: the day any price sensitive information is released to the ASX
9am on the second trading day following the release to the ASX of Waypoint REIT's full year financial results
9am on the second trading day following the release to the ASX of Waypoint REIT's half year result

windows.start_anchor: seven days prior to the date of the annual general meeting
windows.end_anchor: the day of the annual general meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Board may, in its sole discretion, impose one or more further closed periods (blackout periods) by notice at any time, applying to Relevant Persons only or to all employees, subject to conditions and exceptions the Board determines; the imposition of a blackout period is not stated to be confidential, though a refusal of clearance to trade must be kept confidential by the person who sought it.

rules.detail: Derivative is expressly defined to include options, forwards, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars (s761D) and any other transaction limiting economic risk. Clause 7.2 expressly extends the clearance requirement to derivatives over fully vested securities, so an OTC put/call collar is unambiguously in scope.
rules.evidence: Derivative means: (a) derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and (b) any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on protection arrangements over unvested Waypoint REIT securities.
rules.evidence: The entering into of all types of "protection arrangements" for any Waypoint REIT securities (or Waypoint REIT products in the derivatives markets): is prohibited at any time in respect of any Waypoint REIT securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: The same absolute ban extends to vested securities that remain subject to a holding lock.
rules.evidence: is prohibited at any time in respect of any Waypoint REIT securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock.

rules.detail: Once vested and free of a holding lock, protection arrangements require clearance from the Authorising Officer rather than being banned.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires clearance from the Authorising Officer.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not separately named, but the protection arrangements catch-all ('otherwise enable a Relevant Persons to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities') sweeps in a prepaid forward or similar structure; banned while unvested or holding-locked.
rules.evidence: otherwise enable a Relevant Persons to profit from a decrease in the market price of securities.

rules.detail: A monetisation structure with downside protection is a protection arrangement, permitted with Authorising Officer clearance once vested and unlocked.
rules.evidence: otherwise, requires clearance from the Authorising Officer.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short-selling regardless of vesting state or venue.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should a Relevant Persons engage in “short-term” or “speculative trading” in, or “short-sell”, Waypoint REIT securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named, but Trade/Trading is defined broadly enough to capture any transaction involving a change in beneficial ownership, sweeping in a lending arrangement as an ordinary dealing requiring clearance under section 7.
rules.evidence: Trade or Trading includes ... the engagement in any other transaction involving beneficial interest or a change in beneficial ownership of the securities.

rules.detail: CFDs are named and banned only when short-term or speculative; a collar-style CFD position that limits economic risk instead falls to be assessed as a protection arrangement under 9.2, permitted with clearance once vested and unlocked.
rules.evidence: transactions in the derivative markets, involving exchange traded options, share warrants, contracts for difference, and other similar instruments, which are short-term or speculative.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on entering a margin lending arrangement involving unvested or holding-locked securities.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly ... enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Waypoint REIT securities, except with the approval of the Authorising Officer.

rules.detail: Margin lending involving vested, unlocked securities is permitted with Authorising Officer approval.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly ... enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Waypoint REIT securities, except with the approval of the Authorising Officer.

rules.detail: Granting any form of security (charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over unvested or holding-locked securities, to secure the Relevant Person's or a third party's obligation, is banned outright.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security (whether by way of charge, mortgage, pledge or otherwise) over any Waypoint REIT securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Relevant Persons or any third party.

rules.detail: Granting security over vested, unlocked securities to secure an obligation of the Relevant Person or a third party is permitted with Authorising Officer approval.
rules.evidence: grant any form of security ... over any Waypoint REIT securities ... to secure any obligation of that Relevant Persons or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Waypoint REIT securities, except with the approval of the Authorising Officer.

rules.detail: The ban on granting security or margin lending over unvested/holding-locked securities extends to any secured financing for the Relevant Person's own or a third party's obligation.
rules.evidence: Relevant Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Waypoint REIT securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Relevant Persons or any third party.

rules.detail: A loan secured over vested, unrestricted securities (for the Relevant Person's own or a third party's obligation) is expressly permitted with Authorising Officer approval.
rules.evidence: except with the approval of the Authorising Officer.

rules.detail: Blanket ban on short-term or speculative trading, with no defined holding period and no clearance route stated for this restriction specifically.
rules.evidence: Under no circumstances should a Relevant Persons engage in “short-term” or “speculative trading” in ... Waypoint REIT securities.

clearance.tier: All Relevant Persons other than the Chair and his or her Associates
clearance.evidence: All Relevant Persons other than the Chair and his or her Associates | The Chair. Any clearance to Trade from the Authorising Officer must specify the length of any clearance to Trade period and be communicated in writing (including by email).

clearance.tier: Chair and his or her Associates
clearance.approver: The chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee
clearance.evidence: Chair and his or her Associates | The chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee.
the Chair of the Board in the case of directors.

clearance.tier: Employees, contractors and Relevant Persons other than directors
clearance.approver: the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (CEO)
clearance.evidence: the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) in the case of all employees, contractors and Relevant Persons other than directors of Waypoint REIT.
an independent non-executive director in the case of the Chair of the Board.

short_term.evidence: Under no circumstances should a Relevant Persons engage in “short-term” or “speculative trading” in, or “short-sell”, Waypoint REIT securities.

exceptions.evidence: trading that results in no change in beneficial interest in the securities.
the trading occurs via investments in a scheme or other arrangement where the investment decisions are exercised by an independent third party.
a person has no control or influence with respect to trading decisions.

an issue of securities under an employee incentive scheme approved by the Board (however, where securities granted under an employee incentive scheme cease to be held under the terms of that scheme, any trading in those securities must occur in accordance with this Policy).
a transfer of Waypoint REIT securities held in a superannuation fund, in which a Relevant Person is a beneficiary, to another superannuation fund in which a Relevant Person is a beneficiary.
the conversion of a convertible security or an acquisition of the Waypoint REIT securities under a pro rata issue.
undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer, an equal access buy back or a scheme of arrangement.

a disposal of the Waypoint REIT securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, a margin call under the terms of a margin loan against Waypoint REIT securities.

where a Relevant Person is a trustee of a trust that trades in Waypoint REIT securities, provided the Relevant Person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to Trade is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the Relevant Person.

an acquisition of securities under a distribution reinvestment plan or security purchase plan made available to all or most holders (provided that the Relevant Persons did not commence, amend or withdraw their participation in the plan in a Closed Period).
an acquisition of securities on acceptance of an offer or invitation to apply for securities made in or accompanied by a prospectus or product disclosure statement.

an acquisition or disposal of securities under a pre-determined investment or divestment plan for which prior written clearance has been provided ... the plan does not permit the Restricted Person to exercise any discretion over how, when or whether to acquire or dispose of securities.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director/CEO, Chair, or an independent non-executive director (as applicable)
exceptions.evidence: A Relevant Persons may be given prior written clearance from the Authorising Officer to sell or otherwise dispose of securities during a Closed Period where “exceptional circumstances” exist ... severe financial hardship; that is, the Relevant Person can only meet their pressing financial commitments by selling their securities.

exceptions.approver: Managing Director/CEO, Chair, or an independent non-executive director (as applicable)
exceptions.evidence: if the person is required by a court order, or court enforceable undertakings, for example, in a bona fide family settlement, or other overriding legal or regulatory requirement, to transfer or accept a transfer or sell or buy the securities this may be considered an exceptional circumstance.

financing_disclosure: Relevant Person granting security or entering a margin lending arrangement over vested, unlocked securities: requires prior approval of the Authorising Officer under clause 9.4 as part of the general clearance process (section 7); a secured lender's forced sale on a margin call (clause 5.3(e)) is an Excluded Dealing needing no prior clearance provided it does not contravene insider trading law.

exemption_authority: The Authorising Officer (the Chair, or the chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee for the Chair's own dealings) may grant prior written clearance to trade in a Closed Period for exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or legal duties/court orders), with the exceptional-circumstances determination made by the Managing Director/CEO (for employees, contractors and other Relevant Persons), the Chair (for directors) or an independent non-executive director (for the Chair); refusal is in the Authorising Officer's absolute discretion without reasons, final and binding, and must be kept confidential by the applicant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivative means: (a) derivatives within the meaning given in section 761D of the Corporations Act (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars); and (b) any other transaction in financial products that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding the relevant securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy's own definition of Derivative expressly names 'collars', removing any ambiguity that a bank equity collar is within scope and subject to the section 9.2 protection-arrangements regime and section 7 clearance.

bespoke_clauses.topic: clearance expressly extends to vested-security derivatives
bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement includes any proposed dealing in derivatives in respect of fully vested Waypoint REIT securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Confirms a bank collar over fully vested shares needs prior written clearance via the Securities Trading Form and cannot be argued to fall outside the ordinary clearance process.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a disposal of the Waypoint REIT securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, a margin call under the terms of a margin loan against Waypoint REIT securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank's enforcement sale on a margin call is an Excluded Dealing usable even during a Closed Period without prior clearance, provided the Relevant Person is not then in possession of inside information, materially reducing enforcement-timing risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Relevant Persons may not at any time, directly or indirectly, grant any form of security ... over any Waypoint REIT securities which are unvested or subject to a holding lock, to secure any obligation of that Relevant Persons or any third party or enter into any margin lending arrangement involving Waypoint REIT securities, except with the approval of the Authorising Officer.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Confirms the funded collar's loan, secured on vested, unlocked shares, is expressly permitted with Authorising Officer approval rather than banned outright.

bespoke_clauses.topic: blackout clearance extends beyond Restricted Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: all Waypoint REIT Employees (not just Restricted Persons) must seek approval to deal in Waypoint REIT's Securities during a blackout period.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even a non-Restricted-Person employee entering into a collar must seek clearance if a Board-imposed blackout period is in effect at the relevant time.

summary: A funded collar is expressly contemplated: Waypoint REIT's own definition of 'Derivative' names 'options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and collars', and clause 7.2 confirms that dealing in derivatives over fully vested securities requires prior written clearance via the Securities Trading Form from the Authorising Officer (the Chair for most Relevant Persons; the chair of the Audit and Risk Management Committee for the Chair and his or her Associates). The put/call protection-arrangement legs and the security granted to secure the bank's loan are both permitted over vested, unlocked securities with that same clearance (clauses 9.2(b), 9.4), but are prohibited outright while the shares remain unvested or subject to a holding lock (clauses 9.2(a), 9.4). Dealing must sit outside the Closed Periods (the day price-sensitive information is released, the pre-results periods, the pre-AGM week, and any Board-imposed blackout period, which can extend to all employees) unless the applicable approver (Chair, Managing Director/CEO, or an independent non-executive director, depending on role) grants an exceptional-circumstances approval for severe hardship or a court order. If the bank later enforces its security on a margin call, that disposal is an Excluded Dealing available even during a Closed Period without fresh clearance, provided the Relevant Person is not then in possession of inside information, which materially reduces enforcement-timing risk relative to peer policies.
